newsitem.title: FINLAND: Denmark opposes Russian veto on NATO enlargement.
newsitem.headline: Denmark opposes Russian veto on NATO enlargement.

text.p: Enlargement of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) is crucial to the alliance and Russia should have no veto on the process, visiting Danish Premier Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said on Thursday.

"It is a very fundamental cornerstone in the whole construction of NATO that those who are asking for membership and who fulfil the alliance's criteria should have the ability and possibility of being members," he told a joint news conference with Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.
"Russia does not have any veto right as far as enlargement of NATO is concerned," he added.
Rasmussen was on an official visit to the Finnish capital, Helsinki, where U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russia's Boris Yeltsin are to meet on March 20-21.
Yeltsin and Clinton are expected to discuss NATO's expansion plans which Russia says do not take into account its own security concerns.
Rasmussen said there was no list of priority countries for NATO membership and that enlargement should be a dynamic process with many waves of entrants.
NATO founder-member Denmark had no advice for Finland, where there is growing debate over whether to join the alliance.
"It would be very unwise of me, and I think not correct, to give any concrete indications of what Finland's political life and institutions should (decide)," Rasmussen said.
